subject: Recap + next steps: ACME inference evaluation and competitive tests
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Sutherland <sarah.sutherland@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Javier Perez <j.perez@hypcloud.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: ACME inference evaluation and competitive tests

Hi Sarah — great to meet today. Quick recap from this morning's discovery and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Priorities you shared: high accuracy on domain-specific analytics prompts, predictable p50/p95 latency under 200ms for short queries, and strict data handling (no customer PII persisted).
2) You asked for a side-by-side comparison vs HypCloud and a brief POC plan we can run in two weeks.
3) Action items I’ll own: a concise test plan (latency/throughput, hallucination/regression checks using your prompt set, and cost-per-token baseline), sample prompts you can confirm, and a proposed schedule.

Requested from you: the sample prompt CSV (or a pointer to a Drive folder) and confirmation on any redaction/PII constraints for the evaluation payloads.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm prompts (I attached a template) — target: by EOD Monday.
- Redwood runs three test axes: quality (hallucination/regression), latency (p50/p95 under target loads), and economics (tokens + infra).
- We’ll include HypCloud endpoint in the same run so results are apples-to-apples (same inputs, same sequence lengths).

I’ve cc’d Javier from HypCloud so he can pro-actively share any endpoint quirks. Marcus (SE) and Tessa (my manager) will be looped in to scope resources and timelines.

Attachments: acme-sample-prompts.csv (template)

Looking forward — thanks again for the time.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: ACME inference evaluation and competitive tests

Thanks Vanessa — this looks right. A few clarifications: 

- I attached our initial 40 prompt examples (short and long forms) and a small representative dataset; redact any PII before processing — we can provide a sanitized version if helpful.
- Our internal success criteria: false-positive hallucination rate < 3% on named-entity extraction prompts; summary fidelity score >= 0.85 (we'll share scoring rubric).
- HypCloud is already running an evaluation internally; having Javier on the thread is useful so results are comparable.

We can confirm prompts by Monday. Also happy to do a short follow-up call next Wed to review test design.

Best,
Sarah

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Sutherland <sarah.sutherland@acme-analytics.com>, Javier Perez <j.perez@hypcloud.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap + next steps: ACME inference evaluation and competitive tests

Marcus / Tessa — forwarding ACME’s confirmation and their sample prompts. They’ve got two main asks: rigorous hallucination/regression checks and a head-to-head with HypCloud. Can you propose a concise evaluation plan we can run in ~5 business days once they sign off on prompts?

Key constraints/requests from ACME:
- Hallucination target: <3% false positives on named-entity extraction prompts.
- Latency target: p50/p95 under 200ms for short queries (<=128 tokens).
- Data handling: PII must be redacted and no persistent logging of raw prompts unless explicitly permitted.

Suggested tests to include in plan (feel free to rework):
A) Quality: run ACME prompts across three model configs: Redwood (prod model), Redwood quantized (4-bit candidate), and HypCloud reference endpoint. Compute hallucination/F1/fidelity stats using ACME scoring.
B) Latency: 1k short-query runs through each endpoint at steady qps (5 qps and 50 qps) to capture p50/p95/p99.
C) Regression: replay ACME’s historical prompt set to check for known failures.
D) Cost: per-token + infra cost estimate for a 30-day steady-state workload.

Deliverables: test script(s), raw results CSVs, summary slides with clear guidance and recommended config. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ACME-2026-0147. 

Please attach an eval_config.yaml and a short runbook we can hand to the ACME eng team. I’ll track scheduling with Sarah.

—Vanessa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Sutherland <sarah.sutherland@acme-analytics.com>, Javier Perez <j.perez@hypcloud.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next steps: ACME inference evaluation and competitive tests

Thanks — I sketched a practical test plan and attached eval_config.yaml. High-level notes: 

1) Quality evals
- Use ACME’s acme_prompts_v1.csv (40 prompts) plus a 300-item augmentation set we generate by paraphrasing to broaden distribution.
- Metrics: hallucination rate (entity hallucination count / total entities), micro-F1 for extraction tasks, and cosine-similarity on embeddings for semantic QA.
- Baselines: Redwood-prod (fp16), Redwood-quant4 (4-bit int8/4 mix), HypCloud-standard (their default model).

2) Latency/throughput
- Run 1k short-query samples at 5 qps and 50 qps to capture steady-state p50/p95/p99.
- Record token counts and wall-time. We’ll run each endpoint in the same region (us-west-2) to avoid cross-region variance.

3) Regression suite
- Replay historical failing prompts provided by ACME (they said 'short list' will follow). If failures present, capture model logits and decoding artifacts for root cause analysis.

4) Data handling
- For the evaluation: we'll use a sanitized prompt set by default. For any raw PII samples they want to test, we’ll run in a private, auditable job with KMS keys and explicit logging flags per ACME approval.

Resource ask:
- I’ll need access to Redwood dedicated test pool for 2 days (~2x A100 equivalent burst) and permission to run HypCloud calls (Javier, can you share any rate limits or auth details we should expect?).

Deliverables and timeline (est):
- Day 0: prompts confirmed and sanitized (ACME)
- Day 1–2: run quality and latency tests (we can parallelize)
- Day 3: collate results and draft slides
- Day 4: internal review + final deck to ACME

I attached eval_config.yaml and a short script outline. I’ll mock up the result slide template once runs complete.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: eval_config.yaml
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Sutherland <sarah.sutherland@acme-analytics.com>, Javier Perez <j.perez@hypcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next steps: ACME inference evaluation and competitive tests

Thanks team — plan sounds solid. A few quick asks before we kick off: 

- Vanessa: confirm HubSpot deal stage and whether procurement needs a separate NDA / SOW (I see a SOW opportunity link). If ACME wants us to run on raw PII, we need a signed SOW and KMS/HSM details.
- Marcus: include cost-per-query and 30-day extrapolation in the final deck (two scenarios: steady-state 5 qps and burst 50 qps). Also add a short slide describing fallback behavior and suggested SLA tiers.
- Javier: can you confirm HypCloud rate limits and whether they can expose an identical tokenization pipeline for apples-to-apples? If not, note differences in final analysis.

I’ll prep a short talking-points doc for the Wed follow-up call and share before EOD Monday. Vanessa, please schedule a 30-minute working session with ACME and include Marcus for technical walk-through.

—Tessa
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
